title: Private deployment installer story cards and inline help screens
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Goal: Create a cohesive set of visual assets and annotated screenshots for the Private/VPC onboarding flow that can be used in the Console release notes, quickstart docs, and the in-product installer. Scope covers: progressive story cards that guide operators through initial network verification, certificate/KMS setup, agent bootstrap, and non-disruptive upgrade flow; inline contextual help panels for common failure states; and a small screenshot library (desktop + tablet) for docs and marketing.

Background: Customers onboarding Private (VPC/on-prem) repeatedly tell us the install and upgrade steps feel fragmented between CLI, console, and docs. We need an operator-first visual narrative that reduces cognitive load for SREs and platform engineers while matching Redwood's product palette and voice. This work will be used by docs, engineering (installer UI), and the release page for console-2026.03.

Key constraints and considerations:
- Must support both VPC-managed and air-gapped appliance flows in the same asset set (use conditional overlays).
- Screenshots must be exportable at 2x for Retina and include alt text variants.
- Inline help must be short (1–2 lines) and link to deeper docs; use micro-illustrations for four failure classes (network, certificates, auth, resource limits).
- Upgrade modal designs should surface safety checks: preflight results, version delta, rollback window and estimated downtime.
- Keep language neutral for international localization (avoid idioms).

Deliverables:
- 5 annotated story cards (preflight -> network verification -> keys & KMS -> agent install -> upgrade preview) in Figma with component tokens.
- 6 contextual help panels + 4 micro-illustrations.
- Screenshot pack: console pages (installer flow), CLI success/failure outputs, upgrade confirmation modal, and rollback dialog.
- Export-ready image library and a short copy deck for docs writers.

Constraints on uniqueness: avoid duplicating previous private onboarding art direction. This set should be more operator-focused (less whimsical) and use schematic network diagrams rather than full illustrations.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Figma file with labeled pages for each deliverable exists and is shareable with docs/engineering
AC2: Story cards exported as PNG/SVG at 2x with accessible alt text and file naming conventions
AC3: Inline help copy approved by PM and Security with <=90 characters per panel
AC4: Upgrade modal mockups include preflight summary, estimated downtime, and rollback window, and match Console color tokens
AC5: Screenshot library uploaded to Drive with a README describing usage and export sizes
AC6: Design review completed with ENG and PM, feedback addressed or tracked as sub-issues
